question: What is the main goal of program implementation in community health?

options.A: Putting planned health interventions into actual practice
options.B: Gathering baseline data before designing an intervention
options.C: Writing the initial budget proposal for a health project
options.D: Assessing the long-term impact of a finished program

explanation: Implementation is all about action! It means taking the written plan and making it happen out there in the community where people need care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h1)

question: Why can't a nurse just assume a community health program will run on autopilot once planned?

options.A: Written plans are legally required to change every single week
options.B: Daily operational challenges and local realities require constant active adaptation
options.C: Funding is automatically withdrawn as soon as the implementation phase begins
options.D: Community members lose interest before the first day of service delivery

explanation: Fieldwork is full of surprises! Things like sudden shortages mean you have to think on your feet rather than blindly following a rigid script. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h1)

question: Which of these is a must-have before launching any new health program in a community?

options.B: Completion of the final program evaluation report
options.C: Permanent replacement of all local health staff
options.D: Community readiness and willingness to participate

explanation: If the community isn't ready or interested, even the best health plan won't work. Always get the people on board first! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h2)

question: Why do we need to make sure we have enough trained staff before starting a health program?

options.A: To guarantee that administrative tasks take precedence over patient care
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement set by international donor agencies
options.C: To ensure the workforce can handle the service volume without burning out
options.D: To prevent the community from ever questioning clinical decisions

explanation: Matching your team size to the expected crowd keeps patients happy and protects our hardworking nurses from burnout. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h2)

question: When we talk about resource mobilization for a project, what does it include besides money?

options.A: Gathering medical supplies, outreach spaces, and local volunteers
options.B: Closing down existing health posts to save money
options.C: Reducing the number of staff required to run the clinic
options.D: Waiting for international organizations to supply all equipment

explanation: Resources aren't just cash in hand. They include everything from a good venue for outreach to willing volunteers and basic supplies. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h3)

question: A nurse wants women to turn up for a new maternal health clinic. What is the best first move with local stakeholders?

options.A: Rely entirely on radio announcements without speaking to community leaders
options.B: Start the clinic secretly to avoid drawing unwanted attention
options.C: Impose strict attendance fines for women who miss antenatal visits
options.D: Involve local chiefs and women leaders early to help design the rollout

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with respected local leaders builds instant trust and makes community members eager to participate. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h3)

question: What is the main use of an action plan when implementing a program?

options.A: Calculating the total profit generated by the health facility
options.B: Writing the final academic research paper about the project
options.C: Breaking high-level goals down into specific daily and weekly tasks
options.D: Punishing staff members who fail to meet unrealistic deadlines

explanation: An action plan takes big, scary project goals and chops them into bite-sized daily and weekly steps that are easy to manage. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h4)

question: Why should every task on a project checklist be assigned to a specific person?

options.A: To make it easier to fire workers who make minor mistakes
options.B: To ensure only the facility director does any actual work
options.C: To ensure accountability so responsibilities are never neglected
options.D: To prevent team members from communicating with each other

explanation: When everyone is responsible, no one is responsible! Assigning names ensures every important task actually gets done. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h4)

question: Which of these is a daily operational duty in a running health clinic?

options.A: Designing new national health policies in the capital city
options.B: Maintaining proper cold-chain storage for vaccines and supplies
options.C: Conducting the final statistical evaluation of the program
options.D: Securing international grants for future research studies

explanation: Day-to-day operations involve practical care, like making sure vaccines stay cold and clinic traffic flows smoothly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h5)

question: What happens if clinic staff ignore their daily logs and stock registers?

options.A: Patients will automatically receive better care from nursing staff
options.B: The government will instantly increase the facility's monthly budget
options.C: Infection control practices become strictly enforced by default
options.D: Stockouts of essential medicines may go unnoticed until supplies completely run out

explanation: Keeping daily records helps you spot when drugs are running low so you can reorder before empty shelves catch you by surprise. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h5)

question: What does the term 'intervention fidelity' mean in community nursing?

options.A: Delivering the program activities exactly as they were designed
options.B: Writing accurate monthly financial expenditure reports
options.C: Ensuring community members trust the local nursing staff
options.D: Securing loyal financial donors for long-term health projects

explanation: Fidelity simply means sticking to the script! It's about carrying out the health program just the way it was planned to work best. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h6)

question: Why is low intervention fidelity a risk to a health program?

options.A: It automatically stops all funding from reaching the primary health centre
options.B: It makes community members refuse any future medical treatment
options.C: It can cause the program to fail to achieve its health goals even if completed
options.D: It forces the government to shut down the entire health district

explanation: If we skip steps or rush through procedures, the community won't get the full health benefits we promised them. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h6)

question: Which of these is a very common field challenge when running community health programs?

options.A: Immediate willingness of all community members to participate
options.B: The complete absence of any administrative or staffing duties
options.C: Transport breakdowns and logistical delays reaching remote areas
options.D: Excessive funding that exceeds what the clinic can possibly spend

explanation: Bad roads, broken vehicles, and travel delays are classic hurdles every community health nurse learns to navigate. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h7)

question: What is the best way for a nurse leader to handle a transport breakdown during community outreach?

options.A: Wait passively until the government builds a paved highway
options.B: Blame the community members for living in a hard-to-reach area
options.C: Use adaptive problem-solving to find alternative transport methods
options.D: Cancel all future community outreach programs indefinitely

explanation: Great nurses are resourceful! When plans hit a roadblock, we think on our feet and find another way to reach our patients. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h7)

question: What is an important step when moving from running a project to evaluating it?

options.A: Starting an entirely new unbudgeted health intervention
options.B: Organizing and securing all implementation data and records
options.C: Firing all nursing staff who participated in the project
options.D: Destroying all clinic registers to protect patient privacy

explanation: Before you can evaluate how well you did, you need to gather and tidy up all your records and activity notes. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h8)

question: Why is community handover so important at the end of a health project?

options.A: To prevent community members from ever asking questions about the budget
options.B: To legally transfer ownership of the clinic building to the nursing staff
options.C: To ensure local structures keep health activities running after project staff leave
options.D: To permanently cut off government funding to the local health district

explanation: Handover guarantees sustainability. We want the community to keep taking charge of their health long after our project team packs up. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h8)
